gloss: flock; sheep and goats, small cattle
summary: צֹאן is the flock: sheep and goats together, the small cattle a shepherd leads, counted as wealth beside the herd of oxen (בָּקָר), and the source of most offerings, from Abel's firstborn to the Passover lamb. It is a collective, never a single animal (that is שֶׂה), and Lev 1:10 divides it into sheep and goats. Israel is Yahweh's flock, “the flock of his pasture”, scattered by false shepherds and gathered again under one shepherd, his servant David; Jesus takes up Zec 13:7, “strike the shepherd and the sheep will be scattered”, of himself. Arabic ḍaʾn, Akkadian ṣēnu, Ugaritic ṣin and Aramaic and Syriac ʿānā, the Peshitta's word for the flock, all mean the same.

words.summary: About 274 times, always as a collective (with plural verbs and adjectives, Gen 30:38–39; 33:13) and feminine. The one animal of the flock is שֶׂה (1Sa 17:34; Ezk 34:17), and the flock holds both כְּשָׂבִים sheep and עִזִּים goats (Lev 1:10; Gen 27:9; 30:32).

senses.gloss: flock, sheep and goats, as livestock
senses.definition: The small cattle, sheep and goats together, kept and counted as a man's wealth, usually paired with the herd of oxen (צֹאן וּבָקָר); the flock gives milk, wool and meat and goes with the household wherever it moves.

evidence.note: “If his offering is מִן־הַצֹּאן, from the sheep (הַכְּשָׂבִים) or from the goats (הָעִזִּים)”: the flock is both kinds.
“Go to the flock and take from there two good kids of the goats.”
Jacob passes through all Laban's צֹאן, taking speckled lambs “among the sheep” and speckled ones “among the goats”.
Abram “had צֹאן and herd, and male donkeys”: the flock first among his wealth.
His stock was “seven thousand צֹאן, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen”.
Fourteen thousand צֹאן at the last.
The rich man had “צֹאן and herd, very many”, and spared his own flock to take the poor man's one ewe lamb (כִּבְשָׂה).
“With our צֹאן and our herds we will go.”
Pharaoh: “Take your צֹאן and your herds, as you said.”
“The men are רֹעֵי צֹאן, for they have been men of livestock, and they have brought their flocks and their herds.”
Among the blessings, “the increase of your cattle and the young of your צֹאן”.
“Though the צֹאן is cut off from the fold and there is no herd in the stalls”: the loss of all one lives by.
“May our צֹאן bring forth thousands.”
“The hills like sons of the flock (בְּנֵי־צֹאן)”, the lambs, beside the rams.
“The meadows are clothed with flocks.”

senses.gloss: the flock in a shepherd's care
senses.definition: The flock as what a shepherd (רֹעֶה) keeps, leads, waters and defends: the daily work of Abel, Rachel, Jacob, Moses and David, which Yahweh took David and Amos from.

evidence.note: “Abel was a keeper of צֹאן (רֹעֵה צֹאן), and Cain a worker of the ground.”
Rachel came “with the צֹאן of her father, for she was a shepherdess”, and Jacob watered them.
Jethro's daughters fill the troughs “to water the צֹאן of their father”.
“Moses was shepherding the צֹאן of Jethro … and he led the צֹאן to the far side of the wilderness.”
“The youngest … is shepherding בַּצֹּאן.”
“Your servant was shepherding his father's צֹאן, and a lion came … and took a שֶׂה from the flock (הָעֵדֶר)”: the flock, the one animal, and the shepherd who defends it.
Twenty years Jacob kept Laban's flock: “the rams of your צֹאן I have not eaten.”
“Know well the face of your צֹאן; set your heart to the herds (עֲדָרִים).”
“Go out in the footprints of the צֹאן, and pasture your kids by the shepherds' tents.”
“I took you from the pasture, from after the צֹאן, to be ruler over my people.”
He took David “from the folds of the צֹאן … to shepherd Jacob his people”.
“Yahweh took me from after the צֹאן.”

senses.definition: Animals from the flock as offerings to Yahweh: burnt, peace, sin and guilt offerings, the firstborn and the tithe, and the Passover.

evidence.note: Abel brought “of the firstborn of his צֹאן and of their fat, and Yahweh had regard for Abel and his offering”.
“By faith Abel offered to God a better sacrifice than Cain.”
“Of the livestock, of the herd and of the צֹאן, you shall bring your offering.”
For a sin offering, “a female from the צֹאן, a lamb or a kid of the goats”.
“A ram without blemish from the צֹאן” for a guilt offering.
“You shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your צֹאן and your oxen.”
“Draw out and take for yourselves צֹאן for your families, and kill the Passover.”
“You shall sacrifice the Passover to Yahweh your God, צֹאן and herd.”
“Our Passover, Christ, has been sacrificed for us.”
Every firstborn male of the herd and the צֹאן is set apart to Yahweh.
“Every tithe of the herd and the צֹאן … the tenth shall be holy to Yahweh.”
Saul spared the best of the צֹאן “to sacrifice to Yahweh”; Samuel answers that to obey is better than sacrifice (1Sa 15:22).
“All the צֹאן of Kedar shall be gathered to you … they shall go up with acceptance on my altar.”

senses.gloss: a people as a flock: Israel the flock of Yahweh
senses.definition: A people likened to a flock: led, fed and protected by a shepherd, or without one scattered, straying, lost and led to slaughter. Above all Israel, “the flock of his pasture”, whom Yahweh shepherds and will gather again.

evidence.note: “He is our God, and we are the people of his pasture and the צֹאן of his hand”: עַם set beside צֹאן.
“He made us, and we are his, his people and the צֹאן of his pasture.”
“Why does your anger smoke against the צֹאן of your pasture?”
“You led your people like a צֹאן by the hand of Moses and Aaron.”
“Shepherd of Israel, give ear, you who lead Joseph like a צֹאן.”
“Where is he who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his צֹאן?”
“Shepherd your people with your rod, the צֹאן of your inheritance.”
“Yahweh their God will save them in that day as the צֹאן of his people.”
Moses asks for a leader, “that the congregation of Yahweh be not like צֹאן that have no shepherd”.
“I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like צֹאן that have no shepherd.”
Jesus had compassion on the crowds, “like sheep that have no shepherd”.
“All we like צֹאן have gone astray; we have turned each to his own way, and Yahweh has laid on him the iniquity of us all.”
“You were going astray like sheep, but have now returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.”
“My people have been lost צֹאן; their shepherds led them astray.”
“I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
Woe to the shepherds who scatter “the צֹאן of my pasture”; “I will gather the remnant of my צֹאן out of all the lands.”
“Should not the shepherds feed the צֹאן?”: the whole chapter is Israel as Yahweh's flock and its rulers as shepherds.
“I myself will seek my צֹאן … and bring them to their own land, and feed them on the mountains of Israel.”
“I judge between שֶׂה and שֶׂה, between rams and male goats.”
“You are my צֹאן, the צֹאן of my pasture; you are men (אָדָם), and I am your God.”
“I will increase them with men like a צֹאן … like the צֹאן of Jerusalem at her appointed feasts.”
“I will gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together like צֹאן in a fold.”
“They wander like צֹאן; they are afflicted, for there is no shepherd.”
“Shepherd the צֹאן of slaughter.”
“Woe to the worthless shepherd who leaves the צֹאן.”
“Strike the shepherd, and the צֹאן will be scattered.”
Jesus quotes Zec 13:7 of himself and his disciples: “I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.” The Peshitta: ܥܪܒܐ ܕܥܢܗ, “the sheep of his flock”.
“For your sake we are killed all the day; we are counted as צֹאן for slaughter.”
Psa 44:23 quoted of believers.
“Pull them out like צֹאן for the slaughter.”
“Like צֹאן with none to gather them.”
The remnant of Jacob among the nations “like a young lion among the flocks of צֹאן”.

evidence.locator: Zec.13.7, הַצֹּאן → πρόβατα; Num.27.17, Psa.44.23, Psa.95.7, Psa.100.3, Isa.53.6, Jer.50.6, Ezk.34.31 the same; πρόβατον renders צֹאן ×204

evidence.note: Zec 13:7 quoted: “the πρόβατα of the flock will be scattered.”
Num 27:17; 1Ki 22:17: “like πρόβατα with no shepherd.”
Psa 44:23 quoted: “πρόβατα for slaughter.”
Isa 53:6: “going astray like πρόβατα.”
Jer 50:6: “the lost πρόβατα of the house of Israel.”
The good shepherd of Ezk 34 who lays down his life for the πρόβατα.
Isa 63:11: God “brought up from the dead the great shepherd of the πρόβατα”.
Ezk 34:17: the shepherd separates the πρόβατα from the goats.

evidence.locator: 1Sa.17.34, בַּצֹּאן → ποιμνίῳ; 1Sa.16.11, 1Ki.22.17, Pro.27.23 the same; ποίμνιον renders צֹאן ×11

evidence.note: “Fear not, little ποίμνιον, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom.”
“Take heed … to all the ποίμνιον … to shepherd the ecclesia of God.”
“Shepherd the ποίμνιον of God among you.”

evidence.locator: Neh.3.1, שַׁעַר הַצֹּאן → τὴν πύλην τὴν προβατικήν; Neh.3.32 the same

evidence.note: “By the προβατική (the sheep gate) a pool, called in Hebrew Bethesda”: the gate of Neh 3:1.

parallels.note: The herd of oxen, paired with the flock as the two kinds of livestock (צֹאן וּבָקָר).
A flock or drove, set in parallel with צֹאן.

evidence.note: עֶדְרֵי צֹאן, “flocks of sheep”.

parallels.note: Yahweh's people set beside his flock.
One animal of the flock, sheep or goat; צֹאן is the whole.

evidence.note: “Every רֹעֵה צֹאן is an abomination to the Egyptians.”

phrases.gloss: flock and herd: all one's livestock
the flock of (his) pasture: Israel as Yahweh's flock
like sheep that have no shepherd
sons of the flock: lambs and kids

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܥܢܐ (ʿānā), the Aramaic form of צֹאן, for πρόβατον and ποίμνη: the flock as a whole, beside ܥܪܒܐ (ʿerbā), the single sheep.

senses.definition: The flock a shepherd tends and leads; in John 10 and Mat 26:31, the disciples as the flock of the shepherd who lays down his life for it.

evidence.note: Zec 13:7 quoted: ܥܪܒܐ ܕܥܢܗ, “the sheep of his flock”, rendering the Hebrew הַצֹּאן.
“Other sheep (ܥܪܒܐ) I have … and the whole flock (ܥܢܐ) will be one, and one shepherd.”
“The fold of the flock (ܛܝܪܐ ܕܥܢܐ).”
“The good shepherd lays down his life for his flock (ܥܢܗ).”
A servant “who tends a flock (ܪܥܐ ܥܢܐ)”.
Jacob's well, from which he drank “and his sons and his flocks (ܥܢܗ)”.

words.gloss: Zaanan, Zenan: a town of the Judean lowland
words.summary: Twice, a town of the Shephelah, spelled צְנָן in Jos 15:37 and צַאֲנָן in Mic 1:11. Its tie to צֹאן is only the spelling: scripture does not explain the name, and Micah plays on its sound with יָצְאָה “went out”, not on flocks. No cognate bears on it, so its link to the root rests on the consonants alone.

senses.definition: A town in the lowland of Judah, listed with Hadashah and Migdal-gad, whose people Micah says did not go out when the invader came.

evidence.note: “צְנָן and Hadashah and Migdal-gad”, among the towns “in the lowland” (Jos 15:33).
“The inhabitant of צַאֲנָן did not go out (לֹא יָצְאָה)”: a play on the sound of the name.

cognates.gloss: sheep (the wool-bearing kind of غَنَم, as against goats); (ḍāʾin) a single sheep; (verb) set apart the sheep from the goats
cognates.note: Arabic keeps sheep (ḍaʾn) and goats (maʿz) apart under the wider غَنَم, where the Hebrew's צֹאן covers both; the word, its glottal stop and its n are the Hebrew's. It shows ṣ́ (Arabic ḍ) behind צ.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1760, art. ضأن, ضَأْنٌ (n25416)
evidence.note: “[Sheep;] such as have wool, of what are termed غَنَم; one of which is called ضَائِنٌ … the opposite of مَاعِزٌ.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1760, art. ضأن, ضَأَنْتُ الضَّأْنَ (n25414)
evidence.note: “I set apart the sheep [from the goats].”
Sheep; from Proto-Semitic *ṣ́aʾn- “small cattle, sheep”, cognate with Akkadian ṣēnum and Hebrew צֹאן.

cognates.note: The same collective as the Hebrew, “sheep and goats”, and common (over 1,500 attestations). Akkadian ṣ does not show which older sound stands behind צ.

evidence.note: flock; flock (of sheep and goats); sheep; sheep and goats.

evidence.locator: SEM000069 ḍʾn [sheep] N, AKK011045 ṣēnu [flock] N; with HEB006180 ṣoʾn

cognates.note: Ugaritic ṣ does not keep ṣ́ apart, so it shows no sound behind צ.

evidence.locator: SEM000069 ḍʾn [sheep] N, UGC003836 ṣin [ewe] N

evidence.note: Lists Ugaritic 𐎕𐎛𐎐 (ṣỉn) with Akkadian ṣēnum, Arabic ḍaʔn and Aramaic and Syriac ʿānā.

cognates.note: Punic, spelled with the same three consonants as the Hebrew.

evidence.locator: SEM000069 ḍʾn [sheep] N, PUN001711 ṣʾn [sheep] N

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums, the word the Targum uses for the Hebrew צֹאן (Gen 30:31; 1Sa 17:28). Aramaic ע for Hebrew צ is the regular correspondence of ṣ́ (as in אַרְעָא for אֶרֶץ), and the glottal stop is lost.

evidence.note: “small cattle, sheep; (mostly collect.) flock, fold. Targ. Gen. XXX, 31 … Targ. I Sam. XVII, 28.”
The Syriac of the Peshitta, the same word.

doctrine.statement: Israel is called Yahweh's flock: “we are his people and the flock of his pasture” (Psa 100:3; 95:7; 79:13), led “like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron” (Psa 77:21). When its rulers fed themselves and scattered it, Yahweh said, “I myself will seek my flock … I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the lands and bring them to their own land, and feed them on the mountains of Israel” (Ezk 34:2, 11–13; Jer 23:1–3; Mic 2:12), and “I will set up over them one shepherd, my servant David … and I, Yahweh, will be their God, and my servant David a prince among them” (Ezk 34:23–24; 37:24), the righteous branch raised up for David who will reign as king (Jer 23:5). Jesus says, “I am the good shepherd; the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep”, and “there will be one flock, one shepherd” (Jhn 10:11, 16); “the God of peace brought up from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep” (Heb 13:20), and when he comes in his glory he will separate the nations “as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats” (Mat 25:31–33; Ezk 34:17). From the verses: the shepherd is the servant whom Yahweh raises up and sets over the flock, not Yahweh himself, who remains their God; and the gathering of the flock is to the land of Israel, under the son of David, at his coming.

Zechariah's word, “strike the shepherd, and the flock will be scattered” (Zec 13:7), is quoted by Jesus on the night he was betrayed: “you will all fall away because of me this night, for it is written, I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered; but after I am raised I will go before you into Galilee” (Mat 26:31–32; Mrk 14:27). Isaiah says, “all we like sheep have gone astray … and Yahweh has laid on him the iniquity of us all” (Isa 53:6), and Peter applies it to believers who “were going astray like sheep, but have now returned to the shepherd and overseer of your souls” (1Pe 2:25). From the verses: the shepherd struck is a man, Jesus, whom God gave up to death for a straying flock and then raised.

Of men who trust in their wealth the psalm says, “man in honour does not abide; he is like the beasts that perish” (Psa 49:13, 21), and “like sheep (כַּצֹּאן) they are appointed to the grave; death shall shepherd them, and the upright shall rule over them in the morning” (Psa 49:15). Against that it sets one hope: “but God will redeem my soul from the hand of the grave, for he will take me” (Psa 49:16). From the verses: man dies as the flock dies, with no part that escapes; the only way out of the grave is God's redemption, in the morning when the upright rule.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18 from the brief for צאנ. Words: צֹאן (r.ab.ab); the Peshitta's ܥܢܐ (SEDRA lexeme 2364, root 1402), added as a syc word since the brief's Peshitta section searched only צאנ and missed the regular Aramaic ע for ṣ́ (its Peshitta verses found through nt_word: Mat 26:31, Luk 17:7, Jhn 4:12, Jhn 10:1–16); and the place name צַאֲנָן / צְנָן (r.ab.ac; r.cs.ad is BDB's zero-token cross-reference, named so the key is not orphaned), kept as a word since places get no name entry. No personal names are formed from the root. Verse numbers are the Hebrew text's (Psa 44:23, 49:15–16, 77:21, 80:2, 65:14 are English 44:22, 49:14–15, 77:20, 80:1, 65:13; Mic 5:7 is English 5:8). Open: (1) whether צַאֲנָן belongs to this root at all: Mic 1:11 plays on יצא, and the brief's lead derives צֹאן itself from יצא “go out”, which no cognate supports (all show ṣ́ʾn); left in the entry with no cognate. (2) Not followed: Sabaic ẓʾn (Wiktionary; its ẓ would point to ṯ̣, not ṣ́, so not recorded until checked in a Sabaic dictionary), Ge'ez ḥəṣ́an (Wiktionary lists it, but in Ge'ez it is “infant”, not small cattle), Moabite ṣʾn in the Mesha stele (no Moabite source in sources.json yet), and the Amarna gloss. (3) The Peshitta's individual sheep is ܥܪܒܐ, another root; ܥܢܐ also renders ποίμνη in Jhn 10:16. (4) Jhn 5:2 προβατική is linked to Neh 3:1 by the Septuagint's rendering of שַׁעַר הַצֹּאן; the Peshitta there has no sheep word.
